# pane


<!-- WARNING: THIS FILE WAS AUTOGENERATED! DO NOT EDIT! -->

While a turn runs, the chat shows the streaming answer and one line per
tool call. It does not show how many tool calls the turn has made, how
far the plan has got, what each sub-agent is doing, or which files have
changed. The now pane shows these in a narrow column beside the chat. It
shows the present: what runs now, what this turn has done, and the files
the session has written.

The pane is a separate program, `ramabana-pane`, that runs in a tmux
split. tmux is a terminal multiplexer. It divides one terminal window
into panes, and each pane runs its own program. The session and the pane
share information through a file. Up to five times a second the session
writes a snapshot to `now.json` in the session’s run folder. The pane
reads that file and draws it. This page covers the snapshot, the layout
of a snapshot as rows of text, and the viewer that draws the rows and
answers keys and clicks.

## The snapshot

`now_snapshot(agent)` returns a dict that `json.dumps` can write. Its
keys are:

- `at`, the time of the snapshot, and `busy`, whether a turn is running.
- `root`, the foreground turn: its tool-call count (`steps`), how long
  it has run, its state, the call it is waiting on (`current`), and its
  `status`, the last line the model wrote before calling a tool.
- `plan`, the agent’s checklist, with each item’s text and status.
- `subs`, one row per sub-agent. A sub-agent is a second agent that the
  turn starts to do part of the work. The list holds every delegation
  this turn started. It also holds every background delegation that is
  running or has finished since the turn began. A row has the
  sub-agent’s status, its tool-call count (`steps`), its last
  `CALLS_KEPT` calls with results cut to `OUT_CHARS` characters, and,
  once it has finished, its answer cut to `ANSWER_CHARS` characters. A
  finished sub-agent stays listed until the next turn starts.
- `files`, every file written this session, the turns before this one
  included: path, lines added and removed against the file’s text at its
  first write, and the diff cut to `DIFF_LINES` lines. A file whose text
  is back to what it was, for example after `/rewind`, is not listed. A
  notebook is diffed as its cell sources.
- `notes`, what the model wrote before each of this turn’s calls, in
  full and with a timestamp.
- `background`, the work running behind the turn: background
  delegations, commands started with `run_shell_bg`, and folder watches.
  Each row has a kind, an id, a label, a state, the seconds it has been
  running (`elapsed`) and a `detail` text. A finished shell command and
  a folder watch have `elapsed` set to `None`.

The session writes a snapshot up to five times a second (`PANE_EVERY` in
`ramabana.cli`, 0.2 seconds). A snapshot must be cheap to take when
nothing has changed. The list of files is computed again only after a
call finishes. The host is asked for the state of a running background
shell command at most once every `SHELL_EVERY` seconds. It is never
asked again once the command has ended.

Each recorded call (an
[`Act`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#act)) names
the run whose model made it. The `steps` value of a sub-agent is its
tool-call count, the number of calls with its run id. The `steps` value
of the main turn is its tool-call count, the number of calls whose
`parent_action_id` does not name another call in the activity log. A
sub-agent’s calls name the
[`delegate`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/tools.html#delegate)
call that started it. They never count toward the main turn’s tool-call
count.

The example builds an agent with
[`fake_agent`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/testing.html#fake_agent)
and a scripted model, `Root`. The model reads a file, then asks a
sub-agent one question with `delegate_search`. The sub-agent reads the
same file before it answers. The activity log’s `on_change` hook takes a
snapshot when the sub-agent’s read starts. At that moment the pane shows
both agents working. The main turn has taken two steps, and the one
sub-agent is running with one step:

``` python
from ramabana.runtime import current_run
from ramabana.testing import ScriptedBackend, Step, fake_agent

READ = ('view_file', {'path': '/proj/a.py'})
a, _ = fake_agent()
seen = []
a.activity.on_change = lambda act: seen.append(now_snapshot(a)) if not act.done and current_run().kind != 'root' else None
class Root(ScriptedBackend):
    def spawn(self, sp='', tools=(), **kw):
        return ScriptedBackend(self.spec, steps=[Step(tool=READ), Step('a() is defined')], token_delay=0, tools=tools)
be = Root(steps=[Step(tool=READ), Step(tool=('delegate_search', {'questions': ['what does a.py define?']})), Step('done')],
          token_delay=0, tools=a.tools, sp=a.system_prompt())
a._be = a._be_or_none = lambda job='turn': be
list(a.stream('go'))
mid = seen[0]
test_eq((mid['busy'], mid['root']['steps'], [(s['state'], s['steps']) for s in mid['subs']]), (True, 2, [('running', 1)]))
mid
```

Once the turn ends, the sub-agent stays listed as completed. The next
turn clears it:

``` python
test_eq([s['state'] for s in now_snapshot(a)['subs']], ['completed'])
be.steps = [Step('ok')]
list(a.stream('again'))
test_eq(now_snapshot(a)['subs'], [])
```

The plan and the files the session wrote are part of the snapshot too,
each file with its diff. Here the example sets a two-item plan and
changes `a.py` by hand:

``` python
a.plan.set('ship', ['read a.py', 'fix it']); a.plan.update(a.plan.todos[0].id, status='active')
a.before['/proj/a.py'] = 'def a(): pass\n'; a.host.files['/proj/a.py'] = 'def a(): return 1\n'
snap = now_snapshot(a)
test_eq(snap['plan'], [{'text': 'read a.py', 'status': 'active'}, {'text': 'fix it', 'status': 'pending'}])
test_eq([(f['path'], f['added'], f['removed']) for f in snap['files']], [('a.py', 1, 1)])
print(snap['files'][0]['diff'])
```

[`write_snapshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#write_snapshot)
writes the snapshot to a file and
[`read_snapshot`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#read_snapshot)
reads it back. The writer writes a temporary file and renames it into
place. The pane never reads half a file. The reader returns `None` when
the file is missing or does not hold valid JSON. The pane then keeps
showing what it had. The example checks both cases and checks that the
temporary file is gone afterwards:

## Drawing it

`board(snap, width)` lays a snapshot out as rows for a pane `width`
cells wide, one row per screen line. Each row is a `(key, Text)` pair,
where `Text` is a rich styled string. Lines longer than the width are
cut, not wrapped. Use
[`board`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#board) to get
the rows, as the viewer does to find the row under a click. Use
[`render`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#render) to
get something to print. It returns the same rows as one rich renderable.

From the top, the board shows:

- A header with
  [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main), its
  step number, its clock and its status line. The header leaves out the
  call the main agent is waiting on, because the chat shows it. An idle
  agent’s header reads `idle` with the step count of the last turn.
- The plan as a checklist, with the active item highlighted.
- The sub-agents. The first row is
  [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main), with
  the text `talk to the main agent`. Then comes one row for each
  sub-agent: id, status line (or its question when it has none), clock,
  and a mark: `▶` running, `✓` completed, `✗` stopped or failed. An open
  row is marked `▾` in place of `▸`. It adds the question, each recent
  call with its result, and the answer once there is one. An arrow marks
  the row that the terminal is aimed at.
- The files the session wrote, each with its lines added and removed. An
  open row shows the diff, drawn by `hl.diff_rich` with the code
  coloured for the file’s language and the added and removed lines
  tinted.
- The background work: kind, label, state and clock. A row opens to a
  shell command’s last `SHELL_LINES` lines of output, a watch’s pattern
  and last review, or a background sub-agent’s detail.
- The notes, newest first, for reading back what the model said along
  the way. Each is a `▸` row with its time and first line, and opens to
  the whole note wrapped to the pane. The newest note starts open.

Empty sections are left out. A row that can open or be picked carries a
key: `('main', 'main')`, `('sub', id)`, `('file', path)`, `('bg', id)`
or `('note', at)`. The caller passes the keys of the open rows in
`open`. A row stays open when the next snapshot arrives. A running clock
adds the time since the snapshot was written. A long call does not look
frozen between writes. The colours come from the snapshot: the terminal
session writes its active palette as `palette` and its name as `theme`,
so the board draws in the same colours as the main view, and a diff’s
code in the matching `HL_THEMES` style. `ramabana.cli` imports this
module, so this module cannot look the palette up in `cli.THEMES`, and
the snapshot carries the colours themselves. `PALETTE` is the default
`github-dark` palette, for a snapshot written without one.

*The palette `snap` was written with, over `PALETTE` for any colour it

A snapshot of a busy turn, written five seconds before `now`, with every
row closed. The turn’s clock reads 47s: 42 seconds plus the five since
the write:

``` python
call = lambda line, ok=True, done=True, out='': {'line': line, 'ok': ok, 'done': done, 'out': out}
now = time.time()
busy = {'at': now - 5, 'busy': True,
        'root': {'turn_elapsed': 42, 'steps': 7, 'state': 'running', 'status': 'Checking the pane tests', 'current': 'Run shell: pytest'},
        'plan': [{'text': 'Read the viewer', 'status': 'done'}, {'text': 'Rewrite render', 'status': 'active'},
                 {'text': 'Wire the CLI', 'status': 'pending'}, {'text': 'Poll the file', 'status': 'cancelled'}],
        'subs': [{'id': 'run_aaa', 'question': 'which files import fastllm?', 'elapsed': 12, 'state': 'running', 'steps': 2,
                  'status': 'Searching for imports', 'current': 'Search code: fastllm',
                  'calls': [call('Search code: import fastllm', out='agent.py:12: import fastllm'), call('Search code: fastllm', None, False)],
                  'answer': ''},
                 {'id': 'run_bbb', 'question': 'is the pane tested?', 'elapsed': 8, 'state': 'completed', 'steps': 1, 'status': '',
                  'current': '', 'calls': [call('Read tests/test_pane.py')], 'answer': 'Yes, in tests/test_pane.py.'}],
        'files': [{'path': 'ramabana/pane.py', 'added': 1, 'removed': 1, 'diff': '@@ -1 +1 @@\n-from rich.live import Live\n+from teleprint.keys import Parser'}],
        'background': [{'kind': 'shell', 'id': 'cmd_1234abcd', 'label': 'pytest -x tests', 'state': 'running', 'elapsed': 30}]}
def show(snap, open=()):
    con = Console(record=True, width=40, color_system=None)
    con.print(render(snap, 40, now=now, open=open))
    return con.export_text()
out = show(busy)
assert '47s' in out and 'Run shell' not in out and '▸ run_aaa' in out and 'import fastllm' not in out
assert all(len(l) <= 40 for l in out.splitlines())
print(out)
```

Passing the keys of the running sub-agent and the file in `open` shows
the sub-agent’s calls and the diff:

``` python
out = show(busy, {('sub', 'run_aaa'), ('file', 'ramabana/pane.py')})
assert 'Search code: import fastllm' in out and '+from teleprint.keys import Parser' in out
print(out)
```

In an open file the diff is drawn by `hl.diff_rich` in the pane’s
palette. The code in each hunk is coloured by the file’s language, and
added and removed lines get a tinted background. The cell checks that an
added line carries more than two styles. That check shows the code is
highlighted and not drawn in one colour:

``` python
py = {**busy, 'files': [{'path': 'a.py', 'added': 1, 'removed': 1, 'diff': diff_text('x = 1\n', 'def f(): return 2\n', 'a.py')}]}
rows = [t for _, t in board(py, 40, now=now, open={('file', 'a.py')})]
added = next(t for t in rows if 'def f' in t.plain)
test_eq(added.plain, '  +def f(): return 2')
assert len({str(s.style) for s in added.spans}) > 2, 'the code is highlighted, not one colour'
added
```

## The viewer

`Viewer(path, tty)` is the program that runs in the pane. It reads the
snapshot at `path` and draws the board on `tty`. A `tty` is any object
with `read(timeout)`, `write`, `size` and `restore`, as teleprint’s
`RealTty` has.
[`PaneTty`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#panetty) is
`RealTty` with a `read` that returns `None` at the end of input, so the
viewer can tell that its terminal has gone.

The viewer switches the terminal to the alternate screen and asks the
terminal to report mouse clicks. The alternate screen is a separate
screen for full-screen programs. The shell’s scrollback returns
unchanged when the program exits. Each
[`tick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#tick) waits
up to `every` seconds for input and acts on it. The controls are:

- A click on a row picks it, and the mouse wheel scrolls. Picking the
  [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) row
  aims the terminal at the main agent: the viewer writes
  [`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) to the
  [`talk_mark`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#talk_mark)
  file beside the snapshot, and the CLI reads and removes the file, as
  `/talk main` would. Picking a sub-agent row leaves the terminal aimed
  where it was and opens that sub-agent’s transcript pane, which takes
  the lines typed to it. Picking a sub-agent, file, background or note
  row also opens or closes it.
- `j` and `k`, or the arrow keys, move the cursor over the rows that
  open. Past the first or last such row they scroll, so a board taller
  than the pane can be read to its end.
- Page up and page down scroll by a page, and `g` and `G` jump to the
  top and the bottom.
- Enter picks the row under the cursor, as a click does. Space opens or
  closes that row and does not aim the terminal.
- `p` on a background shell command opens a tmux pane below the viewer
  that follows the command’s log with `less -R +F`. `q` in that pane
  closes it.
- `q` or ctrl+c quits.

The last line of the pane is always `HINT`. The main keys stay on screen
however far the board scrolls. Every line is filled to the pane’s edge
on the palette’s `bg0`, and the cursor row on its `bg2`.

Picking a running sub-agent that has a log opens a transcript pane. That
pane is a tmux split left of the chat pane (the snapshot’s `chat_pane`)
that follows the log in the board’s palette, as described under
transcript panes below. The viewer keeps at most one transcript pane.
Picking another sub-agent reuses it. Picking
[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) closes
it. The viewer closes it `PANE_LINGER` seconds (3.0) after the sub-agent
ends or leaves the board, unless the snapshot’s `close_done` is false.
The viewer never closes a pane that it did not open.

The viewer reads the snapshot again only when its file has changed. It
lays out the board on every tick and writes only the lines that differ
from what is on screen. A clock that moves once a second rewrites one
line a second. A board that is not changing writes nothing. When the
terminal changes size, the viewer clears it and draws everything again.

A failed frame does not stop the viewer. If drawing fails, the viewer
keeps the last good snapshot and shows the error as a row until a good
snapshot arrives. However the viewer exits, it restores the terminal’s
normal screen and modes. When the user quits, the viewer leaves a file
named by
[`quit_mark`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#quit_mark)
beside the snapshot (`now.closed`). The terminal session checks for that
file. It leaves a pane that the user closed closed, and it can tell such
a pane from one that crashed. A hangup (tmux closing the pane), SIGTERM
and the end of input count as quitting too.

The example drives a
[`Viewer`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#viewer) with
a test terminal, `Tty`, that replays scripted input and keeps everything
written to it. A click on the running sub-agent opens it and puts the
cursor there. A tick with nothing new writes nothing. Then `j` moves the
cursor down, space opens `run_bbb`, and `q` quits:

``` python
class Tty:
    "A terminal for tests: scripted input chunks, a size, and every write kept."
    def __init__(self, *input, size=(40, 30)): self.input, self.size, self.writes = list(input), size, []
    def read(self, timeout=0): return self.input.pop(0).encode() if self.input else b''
    def write(self, s): self.writes.append(s)
    def restore(self): pass
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
    (p := Path(d)/'now.json').write_text(json.dumps(busy))
    v = Viewer(p, Tty()); v.tick(now=now)
    y = next(i for i, (k, _) in enumerate(v.rows) if k == ('sub', 'run_aaa'))
    v.tty.input.append(f'\x1b[<0;3;{y + 1}M'); v.tick(now=now)
    test_eq((v.open, v.cursor), ({('sub', 'run_aaa')}, ('sub', 'run_aaa')))
    n = len(v.tty.writes); v.tick(now=now)
    test_eq(len(v.tty.writes), n)
    v.tty.input += ['j', ' ', 'q']
    for _ in range(3): v.tick(now=now)
    test_eq((v.cursor, v.open, v.done), (('sub', 'run_bbb'), {('sub', 'run_aaa'), ('sub', 'run_bbb')}, True))
```

## Transcript panes

A transcript pane follows one run’s log, as `tail -f` would, but in the
palette of the main view. Each log line is a time and an entry: `>` a
call, `< tool ok` or `< tool ERR` its result, `~` a status line, `user:`
a line the user sent, and `question:`, `answer:` or `reply:`.
[`transcript_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#transcript_line)
colours one line by that role: the time gray, a call blue, a result
green or red by its outcome, a status gray, the user’s words yellow. A
line without a time, such as the second line of a long question, is
plain `fg1`.
[`transcript_ansi`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#transcript_ansi)
turns lines into terminal text a pane wide, each wrapped and filled to
the edge with the palette’s `bg0`, as the viewer fills the board.

A
[`Follower`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#follower)
holds what one transcript pane has read and drawn. Each
[`tick`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/monitor.html#tick) reads
the whole lines written since the last one, keeping a partial line until
its newline arrives, and returns the terminal text to write: the new
lines, or `''` when nothing changed. It reads the snapshot at `path`
again only when that file changed, and keeps the last palette when the
snapshot is missing or half written. A `/theme` in the main view
therefore reaches the transcript within a tick: a new palette, or a new
pane width, clears the pane and draws the last `keep` lines again. A log
shorter than what was read has been rewritten, so the follower starts
over. The last row of a transcript pane is its input line. While the
snapshot lists a running sub-agent with this log, the row shows `▌` and
the typed text, and the terminal’s cursor rests there, so only the pane
tmux has focused shows a cursor. Enter sends the line to that sub-agent
through the session’s control socket, whose path the snapshot carries as
`control`. The control socket’s
[`tell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/peers.html#tell) calls
[`Agent.tell`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/agent.html#agent.tell),
which `/talk` uses too. The sub-agent’s transcript then shows the line
as `user:`. A refusal, such as a sub-agent that has just finished, stays
on the input line beside the text. A pane following any other log, or a
sub-agent that has ended, takes no input and hides the cursor.
`follow(log, path)` draws a
[`Follower`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#follower)
on the terminal above its input line, waiting up to `every` seconds for
keys. `setup.follow_cmd` is the shell line that runs it, and both the
viewer’s transcript pane and `/watch` use it.

``` python
def transcript_ansi(
    lines,
    P:dict={'bg0': '#0a0c10', 'bg1': '#11151c', 'bg2': '#1c2128', 'fg0': '#e6edf3', 'fg1': '#c9d1d9', 'gray': '#8b949e', 'red': '#ff7b72', 'green': '#3fb950', 'yellow': '#d29922', 'blue': '#58a6ff', 'aqua': '#39c5cf', 'orange': '#ffa657'},
    width:int=80
):
```

*`lines` of a transcript as terminal text `width` cells wide: each
coloured by
[`transcript_line`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#transcript_line),
wrapped, and filled to the edge with `bg0`.*

### transcript_line

``` python
def transcript_line(
    line,
    P:dict={'bg0': '#0a0c10', 'bg1': '#11151c', 'bg2': '#1c2128', 'fg0': '#e6edf3', 'fg1': '#c9d1d9', 'gray': '#8b949e', 'red': '#ff7b72', 'green': '#3fb950', 'yellow': '#d29922', 'blue': '#58a6ff', 'aqua': '#39c5cf', 'orange': '#ffa657'}
):
```

*One line of a run’s transcript as a rich `Text`, coloured by its role
in palette `P`.*

In a light palette a failed result reads in that palette’s red, its time
in its gray and its output in its `fg1`. The board takes the same
palette from the snapshot’s `palette` key through
[`palette_of`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/pane.html#palette_of),
which falls back to `PALETTE` for a snapshot written without one:

``` python
light = {**PALETTE, 'bg0': '#f8f5ec', 'fg1': '#454940', 'gray': '#77776d', 'red': '#9a443b'}
test_eq((palette_of({'palette': light})['bg0'], palette_of(busy)['bg0']), ('#f8f5ec', PALETTE['bg0']))
failed = transcript_line('12:00:01 < view_file ERR no such file', light)
assert {'#77776d', 'bold #9a443b', '#454940'} <= {str(s.style) for s in failed.spans}
failed
```

[`main`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/cli.html#main) is the
viewer’s command line: `ramabana-pane PATH` runs the viewer on the
terminal it was started in. The terminal session starts it in a tmux
split when you type `/pane`, and prints the command when there is no
tmux, so you can run it in another terminal yourself. `--every` sets how
long each tick waits for input. `--log LOG` follows that transcript in
the snapshot’s palette, as a transcript pane does.

[`log`](https://vedicreader.github.io/ramabana/peers.html#log) follow
